html:
Xanana Gusmão led the armed resistance against Indonesian rule and became the first president of East Timor when it gained independence on 20 May 2002.

He took command of Falintil, the guerrilla army of Fretilin, in the early 1980s and united the resistance beyond party lines. Captured in 1992, he was held in a Jakarta prison, from where he kept leading the struggle, until the 1999 vote.

As president, then prime minister, he steered the country through crisis and pushed reconciliation with Indonesia. He led the talks that won a sea boundary with Australia in 2018, giving Timor a bigger share of Timor Sea gas. He is also a poet and painter.
sum: Xanana Gusmão led the armed resistance against Indonesian rule and became the first president of East Timor when it gained independence on 20 May 2002.
